Subject: Request: APAC geo-COLA exception for IC3 SWE candidate

Hi Laura / Marcus —

We have a strong IC3 SWE candidate (Asha Rao, sourcing via GreenLight) based in Singapore. Hiring manager confirms this is the top-of-slate hire for Q3 headcount (HC-2037 approved). Compensation modeling indicates Singapore market median for this role is roughly 15% above our US remote midpoint at IC3 level. The candidate is willing to accept but expects competitiveness to market.

Ask: approval for a geo-specific COLA uplift to base pay of +15% for this hire (Singapore location) and permission to set total cash at the 60th percentile for the role. This would be an exception to the standard remote banding rules — we usually apply up to +8% for APAC.

Rationale:
- Candidate is mission-critical for infra work; manager flagged ramp speed as high priority.
- Singapore market + tax considerations make on-target total comp higher than equivalent US remote offers.
- We have budget in Q3 IC hiring pool (ref: HC-2037) but need leadership sign-off for the exception and confirmation on equity allocation.

I've attached a quick model (col_adj-model.xlsx) with total cash and budget impact across salary + sign-on scenarios. If approved, we'll finalize offer terms and loop in Legal for local tax and payroll.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus: quick comp check and recommended final take-home adjustments (base vs bonus).
2) Laura: formal HR approval for exception and note to update offer template.
3) Stephanie: final sign-off for deviation.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Karthik

Karthik / Laura —

Looked through the model and ran this quickly against Q2 comp bands (see attached comp-bands-2026-q2.pdf). Short summary:

• Base uplift: Singapore market median vs our US-remote midpoint suggests a base uplift of 12–15% to be competitive at the 50th–60th percentile.
• Total cash: Targeting 60th percentile total cash (~base + 10% target bonus) puts us roughly in line with local expectations.
• Equity: Recommend the standard IC3 grant (RSU schedule) + one-time sign-on RSU equal to 10% of the annual grant to bridge LTI gap for local market realities. (See equity-budgets.md for budget headroom.)
• Headcount/Finance: Using the +15% scenario from your model, TCO increase for Q3 (salary + taxes + benefits) is ~USD 17.2k. Finance can absorb within hiring pool HC-2037 but this needs Exec approval for policy deviation.

Risks / notes:
- If we go to Singapore payroll, employer taxes and benefits push TCO higher vs PEO; recommend PEO for speed, SG payroll for long-term org reasons.
- For EU-based remote hires we generally see +5% median uplift; APAC (Singapore) is the outlier and justifies the higher ask.

Attached: comp-bands-2026-q2.pdf, equity-budgets.md (stubs).

If Laura prepares the exception memo, this aligns with Finance numbers and I'm comfortable recommending the +15% uplift and sign-on RSU bridge.

—Marcus
